result.question: What methods could find a length-50 snake-in-the-box in the 7-dimensional hypercube (the proven optimum), or push best-known lower bounds at dimension 9+ (currently 190), beyond stochastic extension and pivot-move search which both plateau at 49? Focus areas: (1) post-2015 snake-in-the-box and coil-in-the-box literature — who holds current records at each dimension and what methods produced them; (2) LLM-guided or program-search successes on combinatorial records (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve, related) and what search-harness designs made them work; (3) warm-start / certificate-seeded record hunting: methods that improve a known-good solution rather than searching from scratch (large-neighborhood search, backbone-guided restarts, solution-space crossover); (4) engineering of canonical exhaustive enumeration for hypercube path problems (isomorph rejection, orbit pruning) — what made the Ostergard-Pettersson exhaustive Q7/Q8 computations feasible; (5) coding-theory constructions for snakes/circuit codes (Reed-Muller-based, necklace/periodic constructions) that build long snakes directly rather than searching.
result.summary: The literature points to three complementary routes past the 49-plateau. First, the strongest post-2015 record method is warm-started Monte Carlo policy adaptation: Dang et al.'s Meta-NRPA (AAAI 2023) set the current d10-13 records (373/721/1383/2709) using a certificate-seeded loop — each new record snake is fed back as the primer for the next 30-minute parallel NRPA run — exactly the warm-start paradigm asked about; notably it matched d7's proven 50 but fell 2 short of Wynn's d9=190, so d9+ records still come from constructive methods. Second, LLM-guided program search (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve, and open-source successors CodeEvolve/ThetaEvolve) has repeatedly set combinatorial records with a transferable harness recipe — evolve a greedy-skeleton priority function (not the solution itself), best-shot prompting, island populations, fast programmatic scoring — and snake-in-the-box satisfies all of FunSearch's stated applicability conditions (fast evaluator, graded length score, isolatable extension heuristic), though no published LLM snake record exists yet. Third, Wynn's 2012 coding-theory construction (circuit codes from permuted copies of an initial transition sequence, where the copy constraint prunes the search) produced the d9-11 records that stochastic search has never matched, suggesting periodic/symmetric constructions are the proven ceiling-raiser at high dimensions. QUBO/quantum-annealing formulations exist (2024) but only reach the d5 optimum and are not currently viable at Q7 scale. No surviving claims covered Östergård–Pettersson-style canonical exhaustive enumeration engineering, which remains the key open gap for certifying Q7=50 by direct search.

findings.claim: Current snake-in-the-box records at d10-13 (373, 721, 1383, 2709) were set by Meta-NRPA — warm-started Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation with optimal stopping (Dang et al., AAAI 2023) — beating the Allison-Paulusma 2016 / Kinny 2012 bounds; but the method did NOT beat records at d7-9 (50/97/188 vs best-known 50/98/190), so Wynn's 190 still stands at d9 and Monte Carlo policy adaptation fell 2 short of it even warm-started.
findings.evidence: Peer-reviewed AAAI-23 paper, Table 5 verified against the official PDF by three verifiers; corroborated by Wikipedia's current record table and an independent 2025 rediscovery of the length-373 d10 snake. Merges claims [0] and [1], both 3-0.

findings.claim: The record-producing harness was certificate-seeded iterative improvement, not from-scratch search: 20 parallel 30-minute NRPA executions, each new record snake fed back as the 'primer' (warm-start seed) for the next execution, looping until no further improvement — with playouts that first replay the primer then extend it, and force-exploration that mutates one choice of the best sequence. This is the directly reusable design for warm-starting from an existing length-48/49 certificate.
findings.evidence: Verbatim from the primary source: 'Each time we have a new record, it is used as a new primer, and a new execution is performed.' Verifier confirmed the parallelism and time-budget details; minor caveat that the record variant was Meta-NRPA with force exploration, not plain NRPA.

findings.claim: Method lineage: evolutionary computation held most snake/coil records until 2012, when Kinny's nested Monte-Carlo search displaced it — finding significantly longer snakes and coils, running faster, and requiring no parameter tuning. The MC lineage (Kinny 2012 -> Meta-NRPA 2023) is now the dominant incomplete-search family, making NRPA-style nested rollouts the natural next step beyond stochastic extension and pivot moves.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [3] and [4] (both 3-0). Peer-reviewed MIWAI/ECAI 2012 papers; verifiers confirmed via independent later literature (GPU-NMCS surveys, Dang et al. 2023) crediting Kinny's NMCS with breaking EC-held records using a single-successor-favoring playout heuristic. Caveat: 'no tuning'/'faster' are the author's own abstract assertions.

findings.claim: FunSearch (Nature 2023) demonstrated that LLM-guided program search can set records on extremal combinatorics problems where classical solvers plateau: it found a size-512 cap set in dimension 8 from scratch (first improvement in ~20 years, beating Edel's construction), outperforming state-of-the-art computational solvers. Its harness has four named, transferable ingredients: (a) best-shot prompting (feed highest-scoring programs back into prompts), (b) a fixed greedy program skeleton where only the critical priority function is evolved — searching for programs that generate solutions rather than the solutions themselves, which the paper reports significantly improves results, (c) an island-based evolutionary population to avoid local optima, and (d) asynchronous parallel scaling with user-supplied evaluator + seed program. Snake-in-the-box meets all three of the paper's stated applicability conditions (efficient evaluator, rich graded score, isolatable evolvable component), so the direct translation is: evaluator = validate snake + return length; seed = the existing extension heuristic; evolve the extension priority function, not vertex sequences.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [8], [9], [10], [14], [15], [16] (all 3-0). Peer-reviewed Nature primary source plus machine-verifiable artifact (published generating program for the 512-cap in the official GitHub repo). Reliability caveat verifiers flagged: only 4/140 runs found the 512 cap set, so per-run success rate is low; cap sets live in Z_3^n not the hypercube, so 'hypercube-adjacent' is loose framing.

findings.claim: AlphaEvolve (DeepMind, June 2025) generalized the approach: an autonomous pipeline where LLMs directly edit code in an evolutionary population steered by automated evaluators, which surpassed best-known solutions on a spectrum of open math/CS problems — headlined by 48-scalar-multiplication 4x4 complex matrix multiplication, the first improvement over Strassen in the bilinear setting in 56 years (independently reproduced and verified). This is evidence LLM program search generalizes across combinatorial record problems, though the paper's own numbers show it improved best-known on only ~20% of its ~50 curated problems, and no snake-in-the-box result is claimed by any LLM-search system.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [11], [12], [13] (all 3-0). White paper (not peer-reviewed) but the flagship result is machine-checkable and was third-party verified; verifiers confirmed the Waksman/Winograd commutative prior art does not refute the bilinear-setting scoping. The ~20% improvement rate caveat tempers 'generalizes' to 'can succeed, not reliably on any given problem.'

findings.claim: Open-source, low-cost replications of the AlphaEvolve harness now exist and are competitive: CodeEvolve (island-based evolution + inspiration-based crossover, meta-prompting, depth-based refinement, CVT-MAP-Elites archive, weighted LLM ensemble) matches or beats AlphaEvolve's reported results on 5/9 benchmark problems and beats OpenEvolve/ShinkaEvolve on 6/9 under matched conditions; with an open-weight Qwen3-Coder-30B backbone it surpassed AlphaEvolve on both CirclePackingSquare instances at roughly an order of magnitude lower cost (~$6 vs ~$35). ThetaEvolve simplifies further (single LLM, large program database, batch sampling, lazy penalties, optional reward shaping) and adds test-time RL — updating model weights during search — which consistently beat inference-only evolutionary search across two models and four open tasks, with RL checkpoints transferring to unseen tasks. Together these show a record-hunting LLM harness is buildable today on open weights at hobbyist cost.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [17], [18], [19], [20], [21]. Architecture descriptions verified verbatim against primary sources (high); but benchmark comparisons are self-reported preprints without independent replication (verifiers noted the AlphaEvolve comparison is against reported numbers, the cost gap is ~6x generously rounded, and evaluator-tolerance discrepancies exist in circle packing). ThetaEvolve's specific 'first to set new bounds' priority claim was REFUTED (1-2 vote) and is excluded; its architectural description and RL ablation survived (3-0, medium).

findings.claim: Coding-theory construction is the proven ceiling-raiser at d9+: Wynn (2012) improved best-known lower bounds for snake-in-the-box coils in dimensions 9-11 and other circuit codes in dimensions 8-13 by generating circuit codes from permuted copies of an initial transition sequence — the multiple-copy requirement constrains the search enough that long codes are found efficiently. Wynn's d9=190 snake bound (the current record) has resisted a decade of Monte Carlo search, including warm-started Meta-NRPA (188), suggesting periodic/symmetric construction plus constrained search, not free search, is the route past 190 at d9+.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [22], [23] (both 3-0). Constructions are explicit, mechanically checkable transition sequences, so the arXiv preprint is adequate; routinely cited in later record surveys. The 'route past 190' inference combines Wynn's method with Meta-NRPA's verified 188 shortfall.

findings.claim: QUBO/quantum-annealing formulations for snake- and coil-in-the-box exist (first published 2024, also solving Maximum Induced Path/Cycle) but are not currently a viable route to Q7-scale records: D-Wave hybrid and simulated-annealing solvers only reached the proven optimum through dimension 5 (length-13 snake in Q5), and the pure QPU (Advantage_system6.3, 5614 qubits, 1000 shots) managed only dimension 3 for snakes and dimension 2 for coils — two orders of magnitude below Q7's length-50 target, with the authors themselves flagging variable-count scalability as the blocker.
findings.evidence: Merges claims [5], [6], [7] (all 3-0). Primary arXiv paper subsequently peer-reviewed at IEEE QCE 2025; verifiers confirmed no QUBO/annealing result at dimension 6+ exists from any group as of July 2026. A negative result for the QUBO route, useful for pruning the method space.

result.caveats: Coverage gaps: focus area (4) — the engineering of Östergård-Pettersson-style canonical exhaustive enumeration (isomorph rejection, orbit pruning) that certified Q7 optimality — produced no surviving claims, so this report cannot say what made those computations feasible or whether they are reproducible/extendable to Q8 exhaustion; focus area (5) is covered only by Wynn's permuted-transition-sequence construction, with nothing surviving on Reed-Muller-based or necklace constructions specifically. Source-quality caveats: the AlphaEvolve, CodeEvolve, and ThetaEvolve results are non-peer-reviewed preprints with self-reported benchmarks (though flagship artifacts are machine-verifiable); Kinny's 'faster, no tuning' characterization is the author's own; FunSearch's headline cap-set discovery occurred in only 4/140 runs, so LLM-search success rates per run are low and the method should be treated as a lottery with a verifiable jackpot, not a reliable optimizer. One ThetaEvolve priority claim was refuted in verification and excluded. Time-sensitivity: record tables move — d10-13 bounds are as of AAAI 2023 and the LLM-harness landscape (CodeEvolve v5 revised May 2026) is evolving month-to-month; circle-packing SOTA has already shifted again (AlphaEvolve V2/ThetaEvolve/TTT-Discover). Applicability caution: no published system — MC, LLM, or QUBO — has set a snake record via LLM program search; the transferability of the FunSearch recipe to snake-in-the-box is a well-grounded inference (all stated applicability conditions met), not a demonstrated result. Finally, the research question's premise (local plateau at 49 in Q7) matches the literature pattern: Meta-NRPA reached 50 in Q7 only when warm-started from strong primers, suggesting the plateau is a seeding/exploration problem rather than a method-class limit.
openQuestions: What specific isomorph-rejection and orbit-pruning techniques made the Östergård-Pettersson exhaustive Q7 (and coil Q8) computations feasible, and is the code or canonical-form scheme available to adapt for seeded partial enumeration (e.g., exhausting completions of a length-40 prefix)?

Can Wynn's permuted-transition-sequence construction be parameterized to emit dimension-7 candidates at length 50 — i.e., does the proven-optimal Q7 snake (or any length-50 snake) admit a periodic/symmetric transition structure that constrained search could exploit, or is it structurally asymmetric?

Would a FunSearch/ThetaEvolve-style harness evolving a snake-extension priority function, warm-started NRPA-style from the known length-48/49 certificates, close the 188-to-190 gap at d9 or find 50 at d7 — and what fitness shaping (record-gap/tail fitness, as in the local autosearch work) best avoids the deceptive plateau at length 49?

Meta-NRPA used lower-dimension records as primers when no same-dimension record was available; is there a principled certificate-lifting construction (doubling/concatenation of a d6 or d7 snake into d8/d9) that produces better warm starts than raw lower-dimension embedding?

refuted.claim: ThetaEvolve is the first open-source evolving-program framework to enable a small open-source model (DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B) to set new best-known bounds on two open problems from AlphaEvolve: circle packing (2.63598308, beating AlphaEvolve's 2.63586276 and ShinkaEvolve's 2.63598283) and the first autocorrelation inequality (upper bound 1.503133, beating AlphaEvolve's 1.503164).
